## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Jāgariya Sutta* ("Wake Up", Iti 47; PTS It 41) is a discourse in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text instructs practitioners to abide wakeful, mindful, alert, centered, sensitive, clear, and calm, and at the proper time to see clearly into skillful mental qualities [SuttaCentral]. T. W. Rhys Davids references this discourse as an illustration of the arahant being described as *sambodhi-parāyana* ("intent on full awakening") [Rhys Davids, Dialogues of the Buddha].
A full parallel to the discourse is preserved in the Chinese canon as T 765.82 (覺悟) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, passage-level parallels are found in the *Smṛtivarga* of various *Udānavarga* recensions (Sanskrit UV 15, UVS 15; Tibetan Uv Kg 15) and Chinese verse collections (T 210.6, T 212.16, and T 213.15) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects extensive internal text reuse in the Pali canon, identifying 67 matching segments across 14 texts [DharmaNexus]. In particular, key phrasing in §2.2_1–2.5 is shared almost verbatim with the preceding *Paṭisallāna Sutta* (Iti 45) and *Sikkhānisaṁsa Sutta* (Iti 46), as well as passages in the *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46), the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), the *Aṭṭhakanipāta* (AN 8), the *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), and the *Lakkhaṇa Sutta* (DN 30) [DharmaNexus].
